card.name: Linking words before a beneficial effect
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as that, to, also, can or may also, right before a verb saying what a food, drug or habit does to the body. Mostly in health-news text and drug-interaction lists.

modes.label: Relative 'that' after drugs
modes.description: The word 'that' after drugs or medicines, introducing an effect on the body.

modes.label: Food benefit claims
modes.description: Words like also, can or to after a food or compound, leading into a protective or health-promoting action.
modes.example: A new study published in the Journal of Nutrition suggests that sulforaphane may<< also>> slow the spread of breast cancer cells.

card.writes: It favors verbs like help and aid, and disfavors words like correction, effect and endpoints.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a sentence is about to say that something helps or acts on the body.
